$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test  # ladder-a
    The root-package check for the module-root corpus runs in normal runs, so it runs after the update: go test ./...
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x

    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/evaluate
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve
PASS
$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./b  # ladder-b-owns
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        outline's probe ran
        outline ran on x
--- PASS: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/outline
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
PASS
$ go test  # ladder-a
    the column parse is owned by . and ./b, each as a lift. Column names are unique per corpus root, and one package owns each column.
        Rename one of the lifts, or remove one. A package that only reads the lift's product gives it to hypercase.Use in place of hypercase.Own.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
    --- PASS: TestCorpus/script
        --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/evaluate
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/parse
            --- PASS: TestCorpus/script/x/resolve
FAIL
[exit 1]

$ go test  # ladder-a-useonly
    the lift parse is used by . and ./b, and no package owns it, so its error is recorded nowhere.
        Own the lift in one of them: give it to hypercase.Own in place of hypercase.Use.
    what ran, in order:
        parse ran on x
        resolve ran on x
        evaluate's probe ran
        evaluate ran on x
